question: Has IGIL's pullback from ₹453.65 reset the Stage 2 chart enough for immediate entry, or do moving-average extension, 5 distribution days, and FII/DII selling require waiting for ₹380.00–₹395.00 with accumulation confirmation?

epigraph.quote: Never chase a stock stretched far above its rising 10-week and 30-week moving averages; let it pull back to weekly support and wait for institutional volume to prove buyers have returned.

web_blocks.title: Stan Weinstein Stage Analysis: Confirmed Stage 2, Extended With Distribution

web_blocks.html: IGIL stays in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 Uptrend across both verified feeds, yet shares remain too extended above moving averages for an immediate buy. On the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger, IGIL closed at ₹431.10 (+2.11% daily, -0.60% weekly, +22.06% monthly, +28.38% 3-month), sitting +19.71% above its rising 50-DMA (₹360.13). Daily RSI(14) read 63.93, with the 20-DMA at ₹417.29, 200-DMA at ₹347.47, approximate 10-week EMA at ₹380.00, and ATR(14) at ₹17.06.

On the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, IGIL closed at ₹432.50 (+0.32% daily, -4.31% weekly, +14.42% monthly, +23.85% 3-month), sitting -4.66% below its ₹453.65 52-week high [43]. That pause cooled oscillators from November 13's 79.69 Daily RSI down to 63.57 Daily RSI, 56.11 4-Hour RSI, and 67.59 Weekly RSI. Volume fell to 9.65 lakh shares, or 0.44x the 30-day average of 22.06 lakh (0.18x 20-day average on the 2026-11-23 ledger) [43]. Even so, live price sits +9.90% above the 10-week EMA (₹393.53), +18.52% above the 50-DMA (₹364.92), +20.69% above the 30-week SMA (₹358.35), and +24.04% above the 200-DMA (₹348.68) [43]. Our timing gate blocks chasing and requires waiting for support.

web_blocks.html: Mapping weekly, daily, and 4-hour shelves proves why buying at ₹432.50 breaks risk math. Our quantitative scanner marks a broad support zone of ₹387.63–₹422.38 around the 20-DMA (₹421.49) and 10-week EMA (₹393.53). Yet against our stress-adjusted ₹480.00 Base Target and ₹349.83 structural stop, buying at ₹432.50 offers just 0.57:1 R:R, and even ₹405.00 offers only 1.36:1. We therefore tighten our actionable entry zone strictly to ₹380.00–₹395.00—centered directly on the rising 10-week EMA (₹393.53), the lower scanner support (₹387.63), and the 2026-11-23 ledger 10-week EMA (₹380.00) [43]. Notice also that our ₹349.83 structural stop sits cleanly beneath the 30-week SMA (₹358.35) and just ₹1.15 above the 200-DMA (₹348.68) as an institutional trend floor.

web_blocks.title: Distribution Days, Sector Rank #28 & Accumulation Confirmation Gate

web_blocks.html: Beneath the Stage 2 label, institutional flow gauges demand extra caution. While IGIL outperformed the Nifty 50 by +23.77% over 63 days and ranks at the 81.4th relative-strength percentile, two yellow flags appear in the ledger [43]. First, IGIL logged 5 stock-specific distribution days in the past 25 sessions (on 0.18x 20-day volume as of 2026-11-23), worse than the broader Nifty 500's 3 distribution days. Second, TheWrap Stage 2 data places IGIL's group at a mid-pack #28 sector rank (41.7% Stage 2 breadth, average weekly turnover ₹471.02 Cr) and flags IGIL as not a Top-25 market leader [43]. Those tape signals echo Screener's shareholding decline in FIIs (10.55% to 8.79%) and DIIs (6.38% to 5.47%) [1].

Broad Indian market breadth as of 2026-11-23 also reads Uptrend (narrow breadth): 55.2% of Nifty 500 stocks stand above their 50-DMA, 48.2% above their 200-DMA, and 7 of 11 sectors trend upward. Meanwhile, IGIL's ATR(14) sits at ₹17.05 on TradingView (₹17.06 on the 2026-11-23 ledger), or ~3.94% of price, with Bollinger bandwidth at 15.06% [43]. Setting our hard stop at ₹349.83 gives a ₹395.00 entry a ₹45.17 cushion (~2.65x ATR, or -11.44%) and a ₹380.00 entry a ₹30.17 cushion (~1.77x ATR, or -7.94%). Because of the 5 distribution days and institutional outflows, we will not buy blindly on light-volume drift into ₹380.00–₹395.00: Tranche 1 requires accumulation volume confirmation (>1.2x 20-day average volume on a green bounce inside ₹380.00–₹395.00) plus a 4-hour momentum reclaim.

web_blocks.title: NO-FOMO TECHNICAL GATE: CASH-EQUITY ONLY, REQUIRE VOLUME-CONFIRMED BOUNCE IN ₹380–₹395
paragraphs: IGIL is not in the NSE Futures and Options segment and has no liquid options chain [46]. Respect the +9.90% extension above the 10-week EMA (₹393.53), the +18.52% live TV gap (+19.71% NSE ledger gap) above the 50-DMA, and IGIL's 5 distribution days. Wait for ₹380.00–₹395.00 with Daily RSI below 55, confirmed by a >1.2x volume green bounce and 4-hour reclaim.

book_paragraphs: Now let us read the tape without emotion—looking beneath the headline Stage 2 label so nothing catches us off guard. Two weeks ago, IGIL was sprinting almost vertically at ₹438.90 with a daily RSI near 80. Since then, shares tagged a 52-week high of ₹453.65 and pulled back 4.31% over the past week. On the November 23 NSE ledger, IGIL closed at ₹431.10 (+19.71% above its ₹360.13 50-day moving average); on the live November 25 TradingView tape, it closed at ₹432.50 (+18.52% above its ₹364.92 50-day moving average).

At first glance, that pause looks tidy: daily RSI cooled to 63.57 on TradingView (63.93 on the November 23 ledger), 4-hour RSI dropped to 56.11, and volume fell to 0.44 times its 30-day average (0.18 times 20-day volume on November 23). Yet digging into the ledger uncovers two yellow flags that rule out passive dip-buying: IGIL has logged five stock-specific distribution days over the past twenty-five sessions—more than the broader Nifty 500's three—and sits inside a mid-pack #28 ranked sector (41.7% Stage 2 breadth) without Top-25 leader status, echoing steady FII and DII selling.

book_subsections.title: Why Chasing ₹432.50—or Even ₹405—Breaks Our Risk Geometry
paragraphs: Check the vertical stretch on the November 25 TradingView snapshot: live price still floats 9.90% above the rising 10-week EMA (₹393.53), 18.52% above the 50-day SMA (₹364.92), 20.69% above the 30-week SMA (₹358.35), and 24.04% above the 200-day SMA (₹348.68). Now anchor our structural invalidation stop at ₹349.83—matching the Stage 2 engine floor right below the rising 30-week SMA and just ₹1.15 above the 200-day moving average.

Buying at ₹432.50 risks ₹82.67 per share (-19.11%) for just ₹47.50 (+11.0%) to our stress-adjusted ₹480.00 Base Target—a punishing 0.57-to-1 ratio. Even our earlier ₹405.00 trigger would yield only 1.36-to-1 against ₹480.00 (and barely 1.02-to-1 on our 54%-OPM stress test). Discipline demands tightening the entry fence downward.

book_subsections.title: Tightening the Actionable Buy Shelf to ₹380.00–₹395.00
paragraphs: Lowering our actionable buy shelf strictly to ₹380.00–₹395.00 locks every rupee onto true institutional weekly support: the rising 10-week EMA sits at ₹393.53 on TradingView, the scanner's lower support sits at ₹387.63, and the November 23 ledger's 10-week EMA sits right at ₹380.00.

Watch how the risk math snaps back into institutional territory inside that band. At ₹395.00 against our ₹349.83 hard stop, your per-share risk shrinks to ₹45.17 (-11.44%, or 2.65 ATRs) for ₹85.00 (+21.5%) to our ₹480.00 Base Target—a clean 1.88-to-1 ratio (and 1.47-to-1 on our ₹461.25 Probability-Weighted EV). At ₹387.63, Base reward-to-risk expands to 2.44-to-1 (1.95-to-1 on EV); at ₹380.00, it reaches 3.31-to-1 (2.69-to-1 on EV).

book_subsections.title: Respecting 5 Distribution Days & Narrow Market Breadth
paragraphs: In an Indian market reading Uptrend with narrow breadth—just 55.2% of Nifty 500 stocks above their 50-day averages and 48.2% above their 200-day averages—individual distribution days matter. Five distribution days in twenty-five sessions alongside FII outflows (-176 bps) and DII trimming (-91 bps) means institutions have been selling into IGIL's post-earnings strength.

Catching a falling knife on quiet drift while funds distribute is how traders get trapped ahead of a sponsor block. That is why we add an explicit proof-of-demand trigger before deploying Tranche 1: once shares pull into ₹380.00–₹395.00 with daily RSI below 55, wait for a green reversal session on greater than 1.2 times 20-day average volume and a 4-hour close back above its 20-EMA.

book_subsections.title: Zero Listed Options Reinforce Pure Cash-Equity Patience
paragraphs: Finally, our options desk check confirms IGIL is not in the NSE Futures and Options segment and carries no liquid listed options chain. You cannot use defined-risk call spreads to ride an extended move while capping downside.

Every trade in IGIL is pure cash equity. Let the weekly Stage 2 trend work in your favor, ignore ₹432.50, demand volume-confirmed institutional buying inside ₹380.00–₹395.00, and keep your ₹349.83 stop non-negotiable.
